governed_construct: A function definition (`def` or `async def`, at any nesting level: module-level, method, nested function). Lambdas are not instances, since Python syntax cannot annotate them.
interpretation: Every function definition in the file must have a return annotation (`-> T`) and an annotation on every parameter: positional-only, regular, keyword-only, `*args` and `**kwargs`. The single exemption is the implicit receiver: the first parameter of a function defined directly in a class body (conventionally `self` or `cls`) need not be annotated, unless the function is decorated with `@staticmethod`, in which case its first parameter is an ordinary parameter and must be annotated. `__init__` and other methods returning nothing still need `-> None`. Annotation content is not judged (any expression, including string forward references, `Any`, or bare `Callable`, counts). Variable annotations and lambdas are irrelevant. A file with no `def`/`async def` is NOT_APPLICABLE; text that looks like a def inside a string or docstring is not a function definition. One missing annotation on any parameter or return of any function makes the file VIOLATED.
